problems.title: Hybrid upper bound depends on summed versus averaged sequence error
problems.source_claim: With appropriately chosen coefficients, hybrid loss upper-bounds conditional diffusion loss without instance normalization
problems.location: PDF p6 Sec4.4 Eq18; p15 Appendix B.3.4 Eqs26-38
assumptions: x0 in R^L; scalar temporal mean and standard deviation
Nonconstant singleton length8 series alternating +/-1, population variance1
Predicted mean1 vs true0; predicted std1 equals true1 and respects proposed cap
Literal standard Euclidean sequence norm versus admissible averaged-MSE convention
problems.suspect_step: Broadcast scalar mean/std errors substituted into vector Euclidean norms without length factors

check.kind: conditional exact counterexample plus alternative analytic proof
check.calculation: Summed Euclidean Lx=8,Lz=0,Lmu=1,Lsigma=0,lambda=3 gives 8>3. Mean-MSE reading gives Lx=1<=3 and is supported by F.mse_loss implementation.
check.result: Literal Euclidean reading false; normalized-MSE reading valid under explicit amplitude caps

counterevidence: Released matsd.py uses unqualified F.mse_loss for sequence and scalar statistics
Code revision is not proven historical experiment commit
problems.impact: The bound is part of core hybrid-training rationale, but intended normalization is unresolved; no supported defect grade or experimental harm is inferred

correction.statement: Mean-MSE bound constant A^2+B^2+1 under |z0|infinity<=A and |predicted sigma|<=B. Summed Euclidean errors admit sufficient constant B^2+L*A^2+L.
correction.verification: Analytic triangle/Cauchy derivation; no adoption claimed

problems.remaining_work: State intended normalization and bounded-predictor domain; reconcile theorem with actual implementation and weights

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The literal summed Euclidean norm and the released averaged MSE are different conventions; the report treats the intended convention and bounded-predictor domain as unresolved.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: The length-eight example yields 8>3 under the literal sum, while the released mean reduction gives 1<=3. Cauchy-Schwarz supplies the averaged bound under the explicitly stated amplitude caps.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Needs Evidence retained: a supported admissible mean-MSE reading prevents assigning a demonstrated core failure to the implementation. No severity is forced from the appendix location or ease of repair.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: Specify loss normalization and caps; the two conditional corrected bounds are verified, without claiming author adoption or historical training validity.

problems.title: Exact Gaussian variational term has a non-isotropic error metric
problems.source_claim: Eq15 denoising objective derived by analogy with DDIM from Eq14 construction
problems.location: PDF p5 Sec4.3 Eqs14-15; background pp2-3
assumptions: Denoiser prediction substituted for z0 in conditional mean
Nonoverlap pair-average K1 with linear interpolation and full-average K2 for length4

check.kind: analytic KL derivation and finite diagnostic
check.calculation: A_t=K_previous-a_t*K_t; exact KL=||A_t(z0-f)||^2/(2 eta_t^2). Equal-norm errors(1,-1,0,0) and(1,1,0,0) both have MSE sum2 but KL0 and13/6.
check.result: Not scalar reweighting of unweighted MSE; ordinary MSE remains a valid conditional-mean surrogate

counterevidence: Paper uses analogy/similar objective wording rather than explicit general KL equality proof
Conditional mean minimizes both unweighted and fixed-PSD-metric losses in unrestricted class
problems.impact: Clarify variational versus surrogate training interpretation; no core algorithm defect established

correction.statement: Label Eq15 as simplified denoising objective; exact KL uses A_t^T A_t. Optimizer equivalence needs function-class and singularity qualifications.
correction.verification: Algebra and conditional-expectation decomposition; not a full ELBO reconstruction

problems.remaining_work: Clarify intended strength of objective equivalence and restricted-model implications

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The exact conditional Gaussian KL uses the non-isotropic matrix metric A_t^T A_t rather than an ordinary scalar-weighted squared error.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: Two errors of squared norm 2 yield KL 0 and 13/6. The source's analogy/surrogate wording is admissible, and unrestricted conditional means minimize both objectives; shared restricted-network optimizers need not coincide.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Needs Evidence retained about the intended derivation strength. This algebraic distinction does not refute the Gaussian sampler, surrogate objective or measured results.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: State the matrix-weighted identity and precise surrogate claim; no additional Major/Minor finding is inferred.

positive_checks.result: Analytically verified; singular K allowed under stated beta/eta conditions

limitations: No benchmark reproduction or training failure claim
No proof of historical experiment commit identity
